blocks.text: I can use ‘en’ to say ‘in’ or ‘by’ and ‘faire’ for different activities in the present tense.
You will also learn to recognise and pronounce [ç/c].
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: to do, to make, to go

blocks.text: [ç/c] is pronounced as in ‘ici’. Read these words and say them aloud.

items: i{ci}
{ci}néma
fran{ç}ais
gar{ç}on
dé{ci}der
{ce}la
mer{ci}

blocks.text: Garçon means boy. Décider means to decide, deciding.

blocks.label: Is every ‘c’ a [ç/c] sound?
blocks.text: No! Not every ‘c’ is a [ç/c] sound. It is just ce, ci and ç.

blocks.q: Each word has the sound [ç/c]. Which spelling does it use?

blocks.text: Être means to be, being. The singular forms of the verb are:

items: je suis = I am
tu es = you are
il est = he is
elle est = she is

blocks.text: We usually follow {être} with an adjective. Il est français.
Add an -e in the feminine form!

rows.note: Il est français. Elle est française.

items.q: Tu es ____ ? (Are you short? said to a girl)
Je suis ____. (I am tall, said by a boy.)

blocks.text: Words in English often have different meanings. Look at ‘pupils’:

items: Pupils get bigger in the dark.
The pupils are talking.

blocks.text: Words can have more than one meaning in French too.
The other words in the sentence (the {context}) show which meaning is right.

items: Je fais un voyage en voiture. = I’m going on a journey by car.
L’acteur parle en français. = The actor is speaking in French.

blocks.text: To choose between ‘in’ and ‘by’, look at the other words in the sentence.

items: Le médecin parle en anglais. = The doctor is speaking in English. (**in**)
Il fait une promenade en bateau. = He is going on a trip by boat. (**by**)
Le garçon est actif en classe. = The boy is active in class. (**in**)
Tu es en France ? = Are you in France? (**in**)

blocks.label: What about the girl who goes food shopping?
blocks.text: La fille fait des courses en voiture. = The girl is going food shopping by car. (**by**)

blocks.q: What does ‘en’ mean in each sentence?

items.text: Je fais un voyage en bateau.
La fille fait un voyage en voiture.
Elle fait les courses en voiture.

blocks.text: ‘Faire’ means do, make and go, but sometimes we can’t translate it literally!
Faire la grasse matinée literally means ‘to do/make the fat morning’! French speakers use it for ‘to have a lie-in’.

items: Tu fais quoi le week-end ? = What do you do at the weekend?
Je fais la grasse matinée le dimanche ! = I have a lie-in on a Sunday!

blocks.text: Use {fais} with ‘je’ and ‘tu’, and {fait} with il, elle or a name.

options: He is going for a walk.

items.q: Elle fait une visite de Londres.
options: She goes on a tour of London.
She does the housework in London.

items.q: Il ____ la grasse matinée le dimanche.

items: [ç/c] is a sound spelling correspondence. Both ce/ci and ç make the sound in ‘ici’.
Être is the verb ‘to be’ and is often followed by an adjective. Adjectives often have a masculine and a feminine version in French.
In French many words have more than one meaning, and the context helps you to know which meaning to use. ‘En’ means ‘in’ and ‘by’.
Faire translates as ‘to do’, ‘to make’ and ‘to go’, but in some expressions it can’t be easily translated.

flashcards.back:
ce, ci and ç.

cela, merci, garçon

flashcards.front: What are the singular forms of être (to be)?
flashcards.back: je suis, tu es, il est, elle est.

flashcards.front: How do you usually make an adjective feminine?
Why can’t you always translate ‘en’ as ‘in’?
flashcards.back:
Many French words have more than one meaning. ‘En’ means ‘in’ and ‘by’.

Use the other words in the sentence (the context) to decide.
To do, to make, to go.

flashcards.front: What does “faire la grasse matinée” mean?
flashcards.back:
To have a lie-in.

Literally it is ‘to do the fat morning’.

flashcards.front: What does “Tu fais quoi le week-end ?” mean?
flashcards.back: What do you do at the weekend?

flashcards.front: Which form of faire goes with je and tu, and which with il and elle?
flashcards.back: Fais goes with je and tu. Fait goes with il, elle or a name.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: What people do: ‘en’, meaning ‘in’ and ‘by’
worksheet.instructions: Use the other words in each sentence to decide what ‘en’ means, then translate the faire sentences and the être sentences.

questions.prompt: What does ‘en’ mean in: Le médecin parle en anglais. (in or by?)
questions.explanation: The doctor is speaking in English.

questions.prompt: What does ‘en’ mean in: Il fait une promenade en bateau. (in or by?)
questions.explanation: He is going on a trip by boat.

questions.prompt: What does ‘en’ mean in: Le garçon est actif en classe. (in or by?)
questions.explanation: The boy is active in class.

questions.prompt: What does ‘en’ mean in: La fille fait des courses en voiture. (in or by?)
questions.explanation: The girl is going food shopping by car.

questions.prompt: What does ‘en’ mean in: Tu es en France ? (in or by?)

questions.explanation: Il takes est, and the masculine adjective is anglais.

questions.prompt: Write in French: ‘You are English.’ (said to a girl)
questions.explanation: Tu takes es, and a feminine adjective adds -e: anglaise.

questions.prompt: Write in French: ‘I am French.’ (said by a girl)
questions.explanation: Je takes suis, and a feminine adjective adds -e: française.

questions.prompt: Translate into English: Il fait le ménage.
questions.explanation: Faire le ménage means to do the housework, and il takes fait.

questions.prompt: Translate into English: Il fait mauvais.
questions.explanation: Faire mauvais is used to talk about bad weather.

questions.prompt: Translate into English: Tu fais les magasins.
questions.explanation: Faire les magasins means to go shopping.

questions.prompt: Translate into English: Je fais une promenade en bateau.
questions.answer: I go on a boat ride.
accepted: I go on a boat ride
I am going on a boat ride
I’m going on a boat ride
I'm going on a boat ride
I go for a boat ride
I am going for a boat ride
questions.explanation: Faire une promenade means to go for a walk or ride, and en bateau means by boat.
